name: saturated-normal-map-dot-shortens-z-to-zero
rationale: The one-texel normal map holds (0.875, 0.9375), so the decode's 2t - 1 gives the exact halves (0.75, 0.875) and air.dot.v2f16 of that with itself is 0.5625 + 0.765625 = 1.328125. That exceeds one, so air.saturate.f16 clamps it and the z reconstruction is sqrt(1 - 1) = 0 exactly, with no irrational square root anywhere. Dropping either dot term leaves 0.5625 or 0.765625, and multiplying the lanes instead of squaring leaves 0.65625; all three take the square root off zero and change the blue channel. The final half-scale-and-bias returns (0.875, 0.9375, 0.5, 1.0), whose distinct red and green also catch a swapped lane.

name: a-snorm-byte-picks-the-style-row-on-both-sides-of-the-boundary
rationale: LandmarkFlat::landmarkFlat_vertex packs the w lane of its normalAndStyleIndex attribute with air.pack.snorm4x8.v4f32, takes byte zero of the result as a signed style index, and reads Building::Style.colors at that index; the half4 it forwards on varying zero is that row. The index is the whole case -- a packing that lands one row away returns an unrelated colour rather than a slightly different number, and all eight rows differ in all four lanes. The eight attribute values are 0.4, 1.4, 2.4, 2.6, 4.4, 4.6, 6.4 and 6.6 divided by 127, so the quantity the pack rounds is those eight numbers and the expected indices are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. Three of the pairs straddle an integer boundary from both sides -- 2.4 against 2.6, 4.4 against 4.6, 6.4 against 6.6 -- so truncation would collapse each pair onto its lower row and rounding away from zero would collapse it onto its upper one; both are visible in three of the eight columns. Nothing here is approximate: 0.1 is the smallest distance any value sits from a rounding boundary, and every colour lane is a multiple of 1/16 that is exact in half, so the half4 the observer widens back to float is bit-identical to the row. The other inputs only have to not interfere: Building::Scale is the identity, Tile::View's first, second and fourth columns make the clip position (x, y, 0, 1), and the attribute's z lane is 1 so the depth lane the shader derives is zero. Each of the eight triangles covers exactly one column's pixel centre of the 8x1 target with 0.05 of clip space to spare on either side, and all three of its vertices carry the same attribute, so the interpolated varying is that column's colour under any barycentric weights.

name: imageblock-slice-block-hangs-off-the-texture
rationale: Four 2x2 tiles over a 3x3 texture: only the (0,0) tile's block fits, the other three hang off the right edge, the bottom edge, or both. Metal decides here whether an imageblock-slice write clips to the texels that fit or discards the whole block, and the pre-filled output shows which. Every value is an exactly representable half.

name: imageblock-slice-copies-the-whole-tile
rationale: One 2x2 threadgroup per tile stages each thread's read into its own imageblock cell, barriers, and then has the (0,0) thread write the slice out. Every value is an exactly representable half, so the comparison is exact.

name: recolour-a-two-deep-volume-through-a-float3x3
rationale: A 2x1x2 volume gives four threads whose z coordinate differs, so the three-dimensional fetch and store are both exercised on more than one slice. Every matrix column and every colour channel is a small integer or an exact binary fraction, so each product and each partial sum is representable without rounding and the fast-math reassociation the kernel is compiled with cannot change the result. Alpha is passed through untouched, and one all-zero texel keeps the transform from being confusable with a copy.

name: select-three-ways-and-shuffle-a-quad
rationale: Fifteen uncovered arithmetic families in one kernel -- air.fast_fmin3.v3f32 (2 case-less corpus sources), air.fast_fmin3.v2f32 (2), air.fast_fmax3.v3f32 (2), air.fast_fmax3.v2f32 (2), air.fmax3.v3f16 (2), air.fmedian3.v4f16 (2), air.max.s.v2i16 (2), air.min3.u.i32 (2), air.pow.v4f32 (2), air.quad_shuffle.f32 (2), air.quad_shuffle.v4f32 (2), air.trunc.f16 (1), air.fast_tanh.v3f32 (2), air.fast_tanh.v2f32 (2) and air.fast_log2.v2f32 (2), 29 sources. Everything here has an exact hand-derivable answer, which is the point: a three-way minimum, a median, a signed maximum and a lane shuffle are all SELECTIONS, so the only way to be wrong is to select the wrong thing, and that is only visible when the candidates differ. The three vectors feeding each three-way call cross each other, so their componentwise order changes with the thread and no lane's answer comes from the same argument twice; a lowering that always took the first, the last, or a two-argument min cannot follow. air.max.s.v2i16 is asked where the two derivations disagree: lane x is t - 3 against 5 - t, negative for the first three threads, and read as unsigned t - 3 is 65533 and the maximum flips to it. Every half is a multiple of 1/2 below 32 and every float an integer or a power of two, so all are exact in their own format; trunc is asked at negative halves ending in .5 and .25 where truncating toward zero and flooring differ. tanh is asked ONLY at zero, because on this host fast::tanh supports no other anchor a derivation can stand on: it does not saturate monotonically, returning 1 at 35 and at 37 and 0.99999994 at 36, and it is not odd, since tanh(x) + tanh(-x) is between 8e-10 and 8e-8 and never zero at all sixteen arguments tried. tanh(0) = 0 survives both, and a lowering answering cosh, exp, cos or 1 - x still cannot produce zero; the argument is u - u rather than a literal so the call cannot fold away. log2 is asked at powers of two the thread index builds. pow is asked only where exp2(y * log2(x)) is exact at every step, log2 of 2, 4, 1/2 and 16 being 1, 2, -1 and 4 with whole-number products. The dispatch is two quads of one simdgroup, so quad_shuffle has a derivable answer rather than a hardware-shaped one, and lanes 0 and 2 are asked so the two quads answer differently.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-four-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 24 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-three linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-multiple-passes-axes-max
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element along axis zero. Every four-lane reduction extent, per-thread count, per-threadgroup count, source and destination bound, broadcast extent, and NDArray size and stride is one, so all loops are bounded by the single authored element.

name: fold-a-zero-function-constant-gate
rationale: A function constant at zero gating the three merge shapes the constant folder resolves, so a wrong answer in any one of them lands in a different row. `mode` is declared at index 0 and supplied as 0, which is also the disabled default the translator models every function constant at, so Metal and the candidate are reasoning about the same value. Row 0 is an UNGATED write and keeps the module past the 'no write survived folding' refusal. Row 1 is written only inside `if (mode != 0)`, so it must still hold its 0xCD fill -- a branch that does not fold writes v * 1000 there, which no other row can produce. Row 2 is an ungated write of `(mode > 0) ? v * 1000 : v - 1`, which lowers to `OpSGreaterThan %uint_0 %uint_0` feeding an OpSelect: a SIGNED comparison of two constants, which the lattice modelled for the unsigned twins only, so before this row's fold the select survived and the answer came from the GPU rather than from the translator. Row 3 is a three-arm else-chain on mode == 1, 2 and 3 whose fallthrough leaves acc at v, so it distinguishes a comparison folded to the WRONG arm from one not folded at all. Inputs 0, 1, -1, 2.5, -2.5, 1e6, -1e6 and 0.5 are exact in f32 under both plus and minus one, so no rounding enters the exact comparison, and v * 1000 is far from v +/- 1 on every lane. The last 8 floats are outside every write and pin the fill.

name: copy-one-geometry-record-the-header-locates-by-byte-offset
rationale:
Metal's software BVH refit kernel, 141 lines, the ONLY corpus host of `native/emitter/body/word_access.rs::emit_join_i32_words_as_i64` and the smallest uncased host of any rule left on the coverage queue. The rule is the read side of an eight-byte record that AIR declares as two `uint` fields and copies with a single `i64` load and store: with no 64-bit integer in the pointee type there is nothing to load, so the value is joined out of two 32-bit words.

One thread. The header's `geometryCount` is 1, so `tid` 0 passes the bound; `refitUpdatesOpacityAndFunctionTableOffset` is set true, so the copy is taken rather than skipped; `geometryOffset` is 256, so the destination record lands immediately after the 256-byte header. The record copied is `opaque = 0x11223344`, `intersectionFunctionTableOffset = 0x55667788` -- two distinct words with distinct bytes, so a join that swapped the halves, sign-extended, or dropped one word would be visible. The whole 288-byte header buffer is the selected region and every byte outside the eight copied is 0xCC, so the case pins the destination offset as well as the value: an off-by-one record index or a byte-versus-element `geometryOffset` would move the write. Every argument AIR marks unused is bound with 0x99 filler, including the two argument buffers and their eight nested pointers, which the reflection requires even though the kernel never reads them. `loop_free`: the entry has no back edge, and nothing here is computed in floating point.

name: pack-four-taps-of-green-into-one-luma-row
rationale: The kernel samples one luma row four times at pixel coordinates 4x+0.5 through 4x+3.5, scales each half to 4095, adds a half, truncates to ushort3 and shifts off the low two bits, then shuffles the twelve components into three 4:2:2 planes. The four source texels carry different values, so the compared plane is exactly the green of tap zero, one, two and three in order -- 99, 297, 699 and 897 -- and a translation that lost a tap coordinate, transposed the chroma shuffle or sampled the wrong channel would write the blue plane's 396, 396, 99, 99 or the red plane's 198, 198, 297, 297 instead. Each half was chosen so its scaled value truncates to the same integer whether the multiply and add stay separate or contract into one fused multiply-add, and so no value sits within a tenth of an integer boundary.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-ten-rgb-lane-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 10 and receives exact float4 zero from all nine linked _uber_clear bodies. name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: visible-table-clear-slot-two-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body without dereferencing callback arguments. Eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds, with register 2 selected as the result. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before its subgroup aggregation path; binding zero is selected for byte-exact comparison.

rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 21 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-three-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-fft-temp-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded FFT work item with unit extents and strides. The destination-temp path confines writes to the authored output allocation. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert. The authored threadgroup allocation bounds the combined-radix scratch footprint.

name: take-a-base-four-logarithm-of-four-powers-of-two
rationale:
air.fast_log2.v4f32 was the largest uncovered symbol in the corpus at 223 sources and had gone unauthored because every host is a 60KB-plus MPSRNN or CNN kernel. A Metal probe first settled the math: fast::log2 is bit-identical to precise::log2 on every input tried - all powers of two from 2^-20 to 2^20, several non-powers, zero, and values at both ends of the float range - so the family is byte-authorable outright.

The host is only large because of a fifteen-way neuron switch that the neuronType function constant selects one arm of. Setting it to 14 picks the logarithm arm and makes every other arm statically dead, and setting input2, input3, input4 and secondaryOutput false collapses the remaining branches, so a single thread runs about 130 instructions: index math, one texture sample, the logarithm, one bounds test, one texture write. input1 is left true so the value being transformed is authored data rather than the zero the phi would otherwise carry - without it the four lanes are equal and nothing distinguishes a vector logarithm from a scalar one.

The sampler is a runtime argument, so the case sets it to unnormalized nearest and the sample coordinate is the thread's own x, which makes each of the two threads read its own texel. The arm computes log2(a*t + b) / log2(c) unless c is exactly -1. With a=2 and b=1 the eight texel values are chosen so that a*t + b is exactly a power of two - 1, 4, 16, 64 for the first thread and 1/4, 128, 256, 1024 for the second - and c=4, so the answers are the eight exact halves 0, 1, 2, 3 and -1, 3.5, 4, 5. One of them is negative and one is zero, and the divide by log2(4) is by two, so a dropped divide or a base confusion moves every lane. The eight output floats were derived by hand; Metal and MoltenVK both answer them.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-sixteen-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 16 and receives exact float4 zero from all fifteen linked _uber_clear bodies. This entry writes the selected zero to both required poisoned output textures, with binding zero captured byte-exactly.
